item.title: Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving
item.description: Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence after admitting dangerously driving his Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon on a motorway. The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later crashed into a metal gate during rush hour, gave no reaction as he was handed a 12-months jail term, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court. Sterling had pleaded guilty to dangerous driving of a Lamborghini Urus and possessing nitrous oxide on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road on 28 May The judge said Sterling's use of the Class C drug had became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period" in his career. Sterling, who left the court without making any comment, was ordered to complete 100 hours unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months. He was arrested after crashing near the M3 in Hampshire. Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence District judge Kirsty Allman told the court on Wednesday that Sterling made a "deliberate and entirely selfish decision" to drive his vehicle "without adequate sleep" and whilst consuming nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas. She said this exposed a "large number of road users to a significant risk of serious harm by the manner of your driving on two motorways and in peak travel time that morning". During the September hearing, prosecutor Simon Jones said a number of calls were made between 07:45 and 08:52 BST about a black sports car and the manner it was being driven. Witness Christopher Jennings called 999 after driving alongside Sterling's car on the M25, and "he was shocked by what he saw", Jones said, and made clear "he sighted the defendant inhaling from the balloon". Fiona Jennings – driving on the southbound M3 – described the driving as "absolutely horrendous" and "swerving in and out of lanes", the court heard. The court heard Sterling strayed into the central reservation of the M3, exited at junction 4A, and veered off the A327, crashing into a metal gate near a layby. His vehicle sustained "substantial damage to the tyres and bodywork and was no longer capable of being driven", the court heard. Sterling was taken to Basingstoke police investigation centre by officers, where he disclosed he had a "problem with nitrous oxide", said Jones. He complied with an impairment test, but for a blood sample, Sterling asked to obtain legal advice before making a decision. In the police sergeant's view "he was deliberately failing to provide a clear answer". Sterling was later interviewed by police with legal representation present where he accepted he had been the driver and provided no comment answers about the driving. item.title: How soon can Giants’ Greg Newsome return from ankle surgery? We asked a doctor
item.description: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will have surgery on his high right ankle sprain. So what does that so-called tightrope procedure entail, and how much time will Newsome miss as the 6-3-1 Giants push for an NFC East title in the final seven games? Well, Newsome will miss at least four weeks since he is now on injured reserve. Could he return immediately after that? That might be a stretch, according to Dr. Kenneth Jung , an orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon at Cedars-Sinai Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine in Los Angeles. Jung, who has not examined Newsome or his MRI results, also works as a foot and ankle consultant for the Rams. Newsome’s reported recovery window is four to six weeks, which could sideline him for the rest of the regular season — with a potential return coming in the playoffs. In his first season in New York, Newsome has become a crucial part of the Giants’ secondary, and his absence for any length of time will be a big blow. Jung called that window “a minimum” time frame. “These can take six to eight weeks to heal,” Jung told NJ.com on Tuesday. “There’s a lot of the soft tissue to heal.” With serious high ankle sprains like Newsome’s injury, the tibia and fibula separate just above the ankle joint, damaging the ligaments that connect the bones. “It’s a little more of a complex set of ligaments, compared to the low ankle sprain [ligaments],” Jung said. That’s why high ankle sprains take longer to heal than low sprains. Jung said a defensive back will require longer to recover from a high sprain, in general, than a lineman because of the nature of his position. As for the tightrope procedure, it involves putting a suture across the tibia and fibula to stabilize them. That type of surgery gained prominence in 2018, when Tua Tagovailoa — then at Alabama — had the procedure after suffering a high ankle sprain in the SEC title game on Dec. 1. He was able to return 28 days later and throw for four touchdowns in a national semifinal win. So why is it called tightrope surgery? “That’s the commercial brand name of the device that’s used,” Jung said. “It’s basically a suture device that you drill across the two bones. Then you insert this device in. “It’s got sutures and two metal buttons. Then when you pull the sutures, it actually squeezes the two bones together — and the buttons hold the bones in place.” With the device securing the bones, the ligaments are able to heal. “While having it in there, it adds stability to the high ankle sprain area,” Jung said. “It’s called a tightrope, but literally, we’re putting sutures across the two bones and then cinching them down.” MORE BY DARRYL SLATER Injured Giants starter needs surgery: Here’s how much time he’ll miss (UPDATE) Nov. 24, 2026, 6:43 p.m. As Giants get major news on starter injured vs. Jaguars, here’s how they’ll replace him Nov. 24, 2026, 12:40 p.m. Jung said a player would “push the envelope” by trying to return from this surgery before the six-week mark, as Tagovailoa did. “Is the

item.title: Drury’s Eckenroth earns at-large bid to cross country nationals
item.description: The NCAA announced its field for the 2026 Division II Cross Country National Championship Monday, Nov. 23, and Drury's Cera Eckenroth received an individual at-large bid to compete at Rim Rock Farm in Lawrence, Kansas, on Friday, Dec. 4. Eckenroth is the first Drury woman to qualify for the national meet since Bradley Weimer in 2022. Her bid marks the fifth national meet appearance by a Panther in DU women’s program history, as she joins Erin Dolan (2012), Claire McCune (2019, 2021) and Weimer. Eckenroth earned her bid with a ninth-place finish in 21:35.2 at the NCAA Midwest Regional on Nov. 21, up 13 spots from her 22nd-place finish a year ago. Two weeks earlier, she placed sixth at the Great Lakes Valley Conference (GLVC) Championships in 21:01.4, 5.4 seconds off the school's 6K record. The junior opened her season by winning the 5K at the Queen City After Dark in 17:06.0. She broke Weimer's program record of 17:23 by 17 seconds and finished 31 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She lowered her own record to 16:52.7 with a third-place finish at the Old Glory Gallop in Dallas. Eckenroth earned All-Region and All-GLVC honors for the second straight season, along with two GLVC Runner of the Week awards this fall. Bergum named GLVC Women’s Swimming Athlete of the Week Drury senior Gwen Bergum earned Athletic Solutions Great Lakes Valley Conference Women's Swimming Athlete of the Week following a strong overall performance against NCAA Division I competition at last weekend's SMU Invite in Dallas. Bergum established a new personal best with her win in the 200 breast — a race in which she claimed one of her two individual NCAA Division II national titles last spring — with a time of 2:10.43, which not only met the NCAA automatic qualifying standard, but also represents the third-fastest in Drury history. She also locked up a third-place individual finish in the 100 breast (1:00.94) and a seventh-place finish in the 200 IM (2:02.01).The Skedsmokorset, Norway native also helped Drury to a pair of impressive relay performances, including a fifth-place finish in the 400 medley and an eighth-place effort in the 200 medley.The GLVC honor is the second for Bergum, who earned the same honor on Jan. 20, 2026. item.title: Oklahoma State “Happy” with 2027 Recruiting Class
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris says he is happy with how the 2027 recruiting class looks just days before the Early Signing Period. The Cowboys are currently around the 45-46 spot in national rankings and sit at No. 8 in the Big 12 conference. Morris told reporters on Tuesday that he hopes to add a few more players before the deadline next Wednesday. The class has already built strong bonds because most of the commits visited campus during the season. Winning games helps the cause, and Boone Pickens Stadium offers a loud environment that recruits love. Morris admitted he usually dislikes in-season visits because coaches get too busy to talk with families. However, the team found a way to make those visits work well for everyone involved. Morris said in a press conference, according to Oklahoman , “Happy with where we’re at.” He added that the town and the game day experience impressed the visitors who came to see the team play. Why the Game Day Vibe Matters The atmosphere in Stillwater is a key reason players want to join the program. Morris noted that the reviews from families who took official visits were very positive. He believes the town and the stadium are major selling points for the recruits. “The one thing interesting is our game day experience is so good, and the town is something I’ve been so impressed with here,” Morris said. The positive feedback from these visits suggests the program is on the right track for future success. Kicker Sam Keltner Wins Big While recruiting is a top priority, the team also has big news on the field. Sophomore kicker Sam Keltner was named a finalist for the Lou Groza Award, which honors the nation’s best kicker. He joins two other finalists: Luke Drzewiecki from Minnesota and Nolan Hauser from Clemson. This season, Keltner has connected on all 50 extra points and 24 of his 25 field goal attempts. He leads the country with 122 total points, and his longest make came from 47 yards away. Morris thinks the numbers speak for themselves regarding Keltner’s chances. “If you look at the numbers with him, I think he’ll win the thing,” Morris said. The team celebrated the news by having Keltner give a speech to his teammates. Morris praised the kicker as a smart kid who will be successful after his playing career ends. Player Health and Injury Updates The team also received good news about receiver Miles Coleman, who left a recent game against Arizona State after a hard hit. Safety Adrian Wilson was ejected for targeting, but Coleman is expected to play in the final regular season game against Kansas. Morris described the receiver as tough and said he is practicing normally. “Tough as nails … Miles is just fine,” Morris said. The coach added that Coleman is running around and making plays just like he always does. item.title: Roger Goodell Releases Emotional Statement Following Death of Martha Firestone Ford
item.description: The Detroit Lions organization is mourning the loss of one of the most influential figures in franchise history. On Tuesday night, the Lions announced that Martha Firestone Ford had passed away at the age of 101. Following the heartbreaking announcement, the Detroit Lions released an emotional statement honoring Mrs. Ford and her decades of dedication to the organization. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell and his wife, Jane Goodell , also released a joint statement Tuesday night, paying tribute to the longtime Lions matriarch. Martha Firestone Ford stands on the sidelines before the Detroit Lions game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 17, 2021, at Ford Field. (via Reuters Connect) Roger Goodell Pays Tribute to Martha Firestone Ford In a statement released by the NFL , the Goodells remembered Mrs. Ford for her commitment to her family, the Detroit Lions, and the city she loved. They also recognized the integrity with which she and her late husband, William Clay Ford Sr. , led the franchise. “Martha was special. She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions – and the game of football – better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions’ organization.” The statement also highlighted Mrs. Ford’s dedication to improving the game of football, her kindness, and her sense of humor. The Goodells concluded by extending their condolences to the Ford family and the entire Lions organization. An Emotional Thanksgiving Awaits the Detroit Lions As reported by NFL.com , Mrs. Ford assumed control of the Lions in 2014 before passing principal ownership to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp , in 2020. Despite stepping away from that role, she remained involved with the organization and continued attending games during the 2026 season. Her passing comes just two days before the Lions host the Chicago Bears in their annual Thanksgiving Day game at Ford Field. What is already one of Detroit’s most cherished football traditions will undoubtedly carry additional emotional significance this year. Our thoughts and prayers are with the Ford and Firestone families and the entire Detroit Lions organization during this difficult time. Rest in peace, Mrs. Ford.

item.title: Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish
item.description: The all-British heavyweight fight is due to take place on 11 December [Getty Images] Councillors have approved plans allowing December's highly anticipated Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight in Cardiff to finish in the early hours. Fans in hospitality boxes at the Principality Stadium will be allowed to drink alcohol until 03:00, with the venue closing at 03:30, to align with prime time viewing in the US. Members of Cardiff Council's Licensing Sub Committee were told 130 police officers would help maintain order at the event on 11 December, with twice the number of stewards present compared to a regular sports event. A handful of residents had objected to the proposed late finish , raising concerns over noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, but none came to the meeting. Councillors were told the event was a "big deal for the city" and would boost the Welsh capital , in terms of "revenue" and "profile." Huw Thomas, chief inspector with South Wales Police, said the challenge for officers was the length of the programme, compared with other events in the stadium, saying the fight was begin viewed by the force as a "three-day event". On Wednesday, the council meeting was told 450 out of the 1600 stewards present on the night would be dedicated to fans seated on the pitch area of the stadium. Mark Williams, Stadium Director at the Principality Stadium, said the ring walk would take place at 01:00 GMT on 12 December, with the fight expected to start at 01:30. Regarding tickets, he said there were still tickets available, but they were "expecting a capacity of 77,000, if everything sells". The boxing rivals are expected to contest the WBA 'super' heavyweight title [Getty Images] Councillors heard objectors had raised "legitimate concerns", but measures had been put in place to mitigate them. Plans for more trains in the early hours of Saturday were outlined, to support spectators getting home after the fight. In response to concerns over noise, the meeting was told "no external PA system would be used" and noise would be "monitored" on the night. Councillors heard initial plans to have live music before the fight would not happen but national anthems would be sung. Regarding alcohol, councillors were told the application was for a "modest two-hour extension on the licence for one night only" and that approximately 10-15 venues were planning to open after hours for fans. Breathalysers would be used on the gates but only for those, "who look worse for wear", according to Williams. After a short period of consideration, chair of the committee, Grace Ferguson-Thorne, said the panel had agreed to grant permission, describing the measures taken - including the stewarding levels and the closure of the roof - as "really reassuring". While early-hour finishes require extensive co-ordination around transport, policing and crowd management in the city centre, the venue already holds a precedent for late-night boxing. item.title: ‘To the moon’ – Blake Griffin hilariously calls out NBA owners over rising ticket prices
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Blake Griffin tackled the recent surge in NBA ticket prices and the overall challenge of being able to watch games for fans. As the NBA continues to earn record-setting revenues with each passing season, the league’s fanbase has perhaps been the most neglected group. New streaming deals that make viewing games on television more unaffordable, combined with the drastic rise in ticket prices, have left NBA fans incredibly frustrated with the product. Blake Griffin suggests NBA owners are driving up ticket prices and viewing costs for personal gain Speaking on ‘The Steppback,’ Blake Griffin tackled the issue of rising costs of enjoying NBA games, both in the arenas and on television. He suggested that the team owners benefit from massive subsidies and an exemption from antitrust laws, thus allowing them to raise prices at the expense of the fans. “You know your prices are too high when the guy wearing $500 of authentic Yankees merch says, ‘Your prices are too high,’” Griffin joked on his show. “And let’s not forget that America’s sports teams at large have received over $30 billion in subsidies for their stadiums and arenas. “So to recap: the teams have a legal exemption to antitrust laws, billions in local subsidies, ticket prices are shooting to the moon, and we still can’t watch the games we want on TV for a price that most people can afford. It’s getting so bad it’s even making bad guys look good. You know… Senator Grayson Allen has a point.” The issue of rising costs associated with being an NBA fan has been a massive issue for several years now. What once used to be an affordable product for people of all ages has now become a luxury good that only the most passionate of fans would be willing to part with the amount of money required to consume the product. Unfortunately, there seems to be no push from NBA owners or Commissioner Adam Silver to try and address this issue. If anything, some owners even relish the opportunity to raise the prices to capitalise on the willingness of fans to pay. item.title: Chris Johnson And Jeff Hafley Demand Answers On Missed Call
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Dolphins lost 26-9 on Sunday, but the final score tells only part of the story. A specific moment in the second quarter has left Miami players and staff furious. Rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and head coach Jeff Hafley both believe a clear penalty was missed against Josh Allen. Johnson was thrown to the ground by Allen, who had grabbed his facemask during the missed call. Johnson stated during a Zoom media session on Tuesday that he was “Definitely surprised there was no flag thrown.” The View From the Sideline Johnson explained the sequence of events that led to the scuffle. He noted that he saw Jacob Rodriguez secure the interception before moving to block. “I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I’m looking for a block,” Johnson said, according to the Palm Beach Post . “It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn’t appreciate it much. And then we got tied up a bit.” Johnson believes the contact crossed a line that should have triggered an immediate penalty. He feels that grabbing a player by the helmet usually results in a flag. “Once you get into another player’s helmet it’s usually a flag,” Johnson said. The lack of a penalty call on this play was one of many missed calls that hurt the Dolphins during the 26-9 loss. Hafley’s Frustration With Officials Head coach Jeff Hafley shared the same frustration as his rookie player. He confirmed that he saw the play and knew his team was upset about the missed call. “I saw it and our guys saw it because they were upset and then they started to talk and I said, I’ll handle it,” Hafley said. Hafley then spoke directly to the referees about the incident. The coach expressed confusion over why the officials did not penalize the roughness. He stated he does not understand how the play was not called a penalty. “And then I asked the refs. I’m not going to get into sending it to the league and everything that happened. I just, I don’t understand how that is not a penalty,” Hafley said. He argued that whatever the play was called, it warranted a 15-yard penalty and a spot change. The Cost of a Missed Call The failure to call the penalty had a direct impact on the field position and the game flow. Rodriguez secured an interception, after which the Dolphins lost 12 yards across three plays until Daniel Carlson successfully kicked a 52-yard field goal. This sequence cut Miami’s deficit to 20-6. A proper penalty would have placed the ball at the Buffalo 11-yard line, a much more dangerous spot for the Bills defense. Josh Allen finished the game with 304 passing yards and two interceptions in the victory. item.title: Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence
item.description: Raheem Sterling has scored 123 goals in 396 Premier League appearances and provided 65 assists [Getty Images] Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there. At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning £325,000 a week at Chelsea. "Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a £50m deal in 2022. "He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example. "He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us." Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal, and commanded combined transfer fees of about £100m. But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work. At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May. The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard. Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis. A stark warning aged 10 Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age. Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead. His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money. Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems. In an interview with the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem." He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison." Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation. With such an accomplished life and so many lives touched, it’s not surprising that there was an outpouring of love from Mrs. Ford online after the news broke. Many teams, media members, former players, and even fans shared their interactions and thoughts about her. Here’s a sampling of them. NFL teams honor Martha Firestone Ford Ford was one of the few female figureheads leading an NFL team. So a few other women in leadership roles around the NFL talked about her being a trailblazer in the business. Here’s Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk: From Titans controlling owner Amy Adams Strunk: "Martha was an inspiration to so many of us throughout the NFL, leading with courage and conviction. For more than six decades, she embodied the very best of what it means to be a steward of our game. Her tireless dedication to the… https://t.co/8weV8jSSSl — Tennessee Titans (@Titans) November 25, 2026 Saints owner Gayle Benson : “I am deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Martha Firestone Ford. Mrs. Ford was a true matriarch of the National Football League and an extraordinary pillar of the Detroit community for more than six decades. item.title: Russell Wilson says young NFL QB is already reminding him of Lamar Jackson
item.description: Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images Lamar Jackson has had a season to forget with the Baltimore Ravens, with injuries hamstringing his 2026 season. Amid his issues, Russell Wilson has admitted there’s a young quarterback already reminding him of the Ravens star. There is an art to being a mobile quarterback, and that is something Wilson knows very well following his time with the Seattle Seahawks. Wilson was one of the most elusive quarterbacks the NFL has ever seen, with Jackson providing a whole different level of agility after being drafted in the 2018 draft. A number of players have since entered the league, adopting the style of a mobile quarterback. Jayden Daniels is one who has particularly impressed Wilson despite enduring his own struggles with the Washington Commanders. Russell Wilson claims Jayden Daniels reminds him of Lamar Jackson Since his rookie season in 2024, Daniels has been unable to avoid injuries hindering his career. This year has not been quite as bad as last, but the quarterback has missed a couple of Commanders games. His stats, however, have been impressive. “What Jayden Daniels did last night, the clutch gene that he had in that moment, took me back to his rookie year when he was healthy and the confidence that he had. I think the biggest thing with Jayden is that level of confidence, that know-how, and that ability to step up and rip the football. He can do it all,” Wilson said on the Set Hut show. “When you think about somebody who runs the football to the pace that he can run with, he reminds me of RG3 when he was a young rookie before he got hurt: that ability to run, he could score at any moment. I also think about a guy like Lamar Jackson with the ability to run like that, but he throws the ball. Him and Caleb Williams, they’ve got great arms. They can throw the ball at any point, at any position on the field. I think that’s the thing that was evident this past game, especially those last two throws of the game.” Wilson spoke about Daniels’ ability to be ‘clutch’ in the moments when the game is on the line; that has taken some work this season after the shambolic ending to the game against the New York Giants. What is worth pointing out is that Daniels has only thrown two interceptions during his eight games this season. Not turning the ball over is something that is priceless to NFL head coaches, with Daniels’ touchdown-to-interception ratio seriously impressive. Bo Nix was heavily praised for keeping Denver in manageable positions despite not necessarily having anywhere near the number of touchdown passes as someone like Joe Burrow. Daniels has shown a lot of ability, which is noted by Wilson, but his ability to keep the football out of harm’s way is perhaps even more impressive. item.title: Kyrie Irving Embraces Supporting Role Alongside Cooper Flagg but Makes One Thing Clear About His Own NBA Status
item.description: Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg © @dallasmavs/X Kyrie Irving gave Cooper Flagg high praise after the Dallas Mavericks’ 120-101 win over the Denver Nuggets. After years of being the spearhead of his teams, Irving is now trying to carve out a complementary role alongside Flagg, who is rapidly emerging as a franchise cornerstone and future superstar. “I’ve played with so many great players in this league. Seeing another young prodigy, a 19-year-old, go after superstardom, I feel like I’m a great complementary piece to that,” Irving said on NBA Showtime after the game. Irving said he knows exactly what his job is and what he brings to the table. “But I’m also established in this league myself. I don’t feel like a lot of people can guard me,” Irving added. The nine-time All-Star has been a stabilizing presence and, at times, a mentor to younger players, including Flagg, who burst onto the scene last year. While Irving missed the entire previous season with injuries, he’s now showing what he’s capable of. He’s averaging 22.0 points on 45.9% shooting in 14 games, while Flagg leads the team in points (24.3), assists (6.4) and steals (1.9). Flagg had another double-double against the Nuggets, finishing with 24 points, 12 assists and six rebounds. Irving, meanwhile, had an off night offensively, finishing with 11 points on 5-of-19 shooting from the field, including 1-of-8 from beyond the arc. Kyrie Irving’s Leadership Earns Praise From Hall of Famer Throughout his career, Kyrie Irving has played alongside some of the best players in NBA history. From winning a championship with LeBron James to reaching the NBA Finals with Luka Doncic, and now sharing the court with Cooper Flagg, Irving has experienced plenty of different team environments. Following the game, Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony highlighted Irving’s ability to balance his leadership by being more vocal and leading by example. “I love to see this Kyrie. When you talk about the amount of work Kyrie puts into his craft, and someone who’s been there with him and spent summers with him. Understand the attention to detail that he has, he’s confrontational in the (summer) workouts, so I can imagine what he’s doing in the locker room with those guys, a younger group who doesn’t have the experience Kyrie has. I love when he said we’re confrontational. That’s not a bad thing, that’s just we’re putting everything out on the table, no side talk. We’re men at the end of the day, so if your whole locker room is operating like that, then it’s a beautiful locker room,” Anthony said via @MavsFilmRoom on X. It’s part of what makes Irving such an effective leader, and such communication is crucial to building team chemistry. Continually improving as individual players while developing stronger chemistry could help the Mavericks slowly but surely transition out of their rebuild over the next few seasons. item.title: NASCAR Fans Angry at Trackhouse Over Bizarre Connor Zilisch’s New AI-Powered Race Car
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trackhouse Racing has found a way to make a NASCAR race car talk. Not through a driver on the radio or a crew chief explaining what is happening, but through artificial intelligence. The team’s new 88Bot gives Connor Zilisch’s No.88 Chevrolet its own personality, allowing users to ask questions and receive updates based on what is happening during a race. It is an ambitious technology project, but some fans aren’t exactly impressed. The reaction on X has been overwhelmingly negative. “This is so bad NASCAR needs to ban this,” one fan wrote. Another had a more direct suggestion for Trackhouse: “How about trying to make the cars faster?” Others questioned the idea altogether, with comments including “what are we even doing” and “wt* man.” It’s easy to see where the frustration comes from. Zilisch’s first full-time Cup season has been a rough one: 33rd in the 2026 standings, two top 10s and 10 DNFs. With that as the backdrop, plenty of fans would rather see Trackhouse put its energy into getting the car running better than into another tech showpiece. Trackhouse’s AI car can process 25,000 data messages per second May 10, 2026; Watkins Glen, New York, USA; Crew members push the car of NASCAR Cup Series driver Connor Zilisch (88) to pit road prior to the Go Bowling at The Glen at Watkins Glen International. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O’Haren-Imagn Images There’s a lot more to 88Bot than a chatbot pretending to be a race car. Trackhouse built it with digital design firm Very Good Ventures, and it runs on the same real-time data setup the team uses to process information from its cars during races. It can handle roughly 25,000 data messages per second, using live telemetry to answer questions and give updates. The AI is built to talk as if it’s the No.88 Chevrolet itself. It can tell you where it is, what’s going on around it and how the race is unfolding, rather than just reading out a list of stats. It also uses voice technology from LiveKit, and it was developed across the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with testing at events including Daytona and the Enjoy Illinois 300. The goal is to give guests a new way to follow the race. Instead of staring at a screen full of numbers, they can ask the car questions and get answers based on what’s happening on track. A VIP experience, not something every NASCAR fan gets The most frustrating thing about the project may be who it was built for. Trackhouse and Very Good Ventures have been working together on a digital experience for guests in the team’s pit box. The companion app, built with Flutter, pulls race information, telemetry, video and other team content together across multiple devices. 88Bot takes that a step further by letting guests talk to the car itself. The decision comes just one day after Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy publicly backed Rodgers, telling reporters that the four-time NFL MVP remained the team’s quarterback. According to ESPN’s Brooke Pryor, the decision to bench Rodgers was performance-related rather than injury-related. For Detroit Lions fans who spent years watching Rodgers torment the NFC North as quarterback of the Green Bay Packers, it is a remarkable development. Rodgers, who will turn 43 next week, previously announced that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL. Rodgers has completed just 60.9% of his passes this season while taking 31 sacks, resulting in an NFL-worst 257 yards lost. Perhaps even more concerning is Rodgers’ declining accuracy. His 18.9% off-target rate ranks 28th among 30 qualified NFL quarterbacks, a stunning statistic for a player whose pinpoint accuracy helped make him one of the most dangerous passers in league history. The irony is that Rodgers helped bring McCarthy to Pittsburgh, recommending that general manager Omar Khan consider his former Packers head coach during the team’s coaching search. Now, the coach who helped Rodgers become a superstar in Green Bay is the same man making the decision to take him out of the starting lineup. Has Aaron Rodgers Played His Final NFL Snap? That is now the biggest question surrounding Rodgers, whose future could depend on how Rudolph performs down the stretch. Rudolph previously demonstrated his ability to provide Pittsburgh with an offensive spark, winning three consecutive games as the team’s starter to close out the 2023 regular season. Rodgers spent much of his career making life miserable for Lions fans, but there is no denying what he accomplished during his 22-year NFL career. Four MVP awards, a Super Bowl championship and a virtually guaranteed spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame speak for themselves. Every legendary quarterback eventually reaches the end of the road. For Rodgers, that moment may have arrived sooner than he anticipated.

item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
